title: Course add and drop
text: Students may add a course through 17:00 on teaching day 5, subject to available seats and prerequisites. A course dropped by 17:00 on teaching day 10 does not appear on the transcript. Later withdrawal follows the withdrawal policy. Advisors cannot override a full class without written department approval.

title: Course withdrawal
text: After the drop period, students may withdraw through the end of teaching week 8. An approved withdrawal records W and does not affect GPA. Withdrawal after week 8 requires documented exceptional circumstances and approval by the Academic Review Panel. Nonattendance is not a withdrawal request.

title: Attendance and absence
text: Students should attend all scheduled classes. After three unexcused absences in a course, the instructor sends a written warning. A fourth unexcused absence triggers an advisor meeting, not automatic failure. Evidence for an excused absence should be submitted within five working days of return. Individual laboratory safety attendance requirements may be stricter.

title: Assessment extension
text: A student requesting an assessment extension should apply at least 48 hours before the deadline with an explanation. The instructor may approve up to seven calendar days. Sudden emergencies may be reported within two working days after the deadline. Extensions longer than seven days require the department chair. An extension does not change an examination date.

title: Grade appeal
text: A grade appeal must be filed within ten working days after the grade is released. The student first requests an explanation from the instructor and then submits evidence of a marking or procedural error to the department chair. Disagreement alone is insufficient. The chair normally responds within fifteen working days; a subsequent panel review may increase or decrease the grade.

title: Academic integrity and AI
text: Generative AI use is permitted only when the assessment instructions explicitly allow it. Students must declare the tool, purpose, and material contribution. Fabricated references, undisclosed AI-written assessed work, and submitting another person's work are prohibited. Instructors explain allowed assistance before assessment. Suspected violations receive a documented review and an opportunity for the student to respond; this policy does not prescribe automatic expulsion.

title: Tuition installment plan
text: Students may request three equal tuition installments before the semester payment deadline. Approval requires no overdue balance from an earlier semester. Installments are due on teaching days 1, 30, and 60. A missed installment triggers an email notice and a five-working-day grace period. The plan covers tuition only, excluding housing and meal charges.

title: Tuition refund
text: A full tuition refund is available for complete semester cancellation before teaching day 1. Cancellation during teaching days 1–10 receives 75 percent; days 11–20 receives 50 percent. No routine tuition refund is available after day 20. The application fee is nonrefundable. Approved exceptional refunds are reviewed separately and are not guaranteed.

title: Emergency hardship grant
text: Students facing an unexpected essential living expense may apply for a hardship grant of up to 1200 campus credits once per academic year. The application requires a short budget and supporting evidence; academic performance is not a ranking criterion. A support officer normally decides within seven working days. The grant is not a loan and has no guaranteed approval.

title: Scholarship renewal
text: A merit scholarship renews when the student completes at least 24 credits in the academic year and maintains a cumulative GPA of 3.20 or higher. A student below either threshold may request one semester of probation with an improvement plan. Renewal is reviewed annually. Hardship grants use different eligibility rules and do not require this GPA.

title: Residence quiet hours
text: Residence quiet hours run from 22:00 to 08:00 Sunday through Thursday and 00:00 to 09:00 Friday and Saturday. During the published examination period, quiet hours apply all day. Residents should first contact the duty resident assistant for noise concerns. Repeated breaches are reviewed by Housing with notice and an opportunity to respond.

title: Overnight guests
text: An overnight guest must be registered with Housing at least 24 hours before arrival and have the roommate's consent. A resident may host a guest for at most two consecutive nights and six nights per calendar month. Guests must be at least 18 and carry identification. Hosts remain responsible for guest conduct. Approval does not provide access to other residence rooms.

title: Housing maintenance
text: Residents submit routine maintenance requests through the housing portal with the location and description. Housing acknowledges routine tickets within two working days; this is not a guaranteed repair deadline. Water leaks near electricity, smoke, and exposed live wires require immediate contact with campus emergency security. Residents should not attempt electrical repairs.

title: Library borrowing
text: Undergraduates may borrow eight books for 21 calendar days; postgraduates may borrow twelve books for 28 days. Two renewals are allowed unless another reader has reserved the item. Reference books remain in the library. Lost books require replacement or the current replacement charge. Borrowing entitlement does not grant redistribution rights over digital resources.

title: Library study rooms
text: Groups of two to six students may reserve a study room for up to two hours per day. Reservations open seven days in advance. A booking is released after fifteen minutes if the group has not checked in. Rooms are for study and may not be used for commercial tutoring. Accessibility needs can be discussed with the library service desk.

title: IT password reset
text: Students reset account passwords using the self-service identity portal and an enrolled second factor. If the second factor is unavailable, the service desk verifies identity in person or through an approved video appointment. Staff will never ask for a password or authentication code by email. Temporary access codes expire after 30 minutes. This policy does not reveal anyone's credentials.

title: Lost device response
text: A lost device with campus email or files should be reported to IT Security within one hour of discovery. The owner should revoke active sessions and change the account password from a trusted device. IT may remove institutional data from managed devices according to the device agreement. Report theft to security as well. Do not post passwords in a support ticket.

title: Student record privacy
text: Students may inspect their own education records through the registrar portal. A record correction request receives an initial response within ten working days. Personal records are released to a third party only with the student's written consent or an applicable legal basis assessed by the privacy officer. Public policy information does not authorize disclosure of grades, identification numbers, or disciplinary histories.

title: Accessibility adjustments
text: Students may request reasonable academic adjustments through a confidential accessibility appointment. Functional needs evidence is reviewed by an accessibility officer; instructors receive approved adjustments, not diagnostic details. Requests should be made at least ten working days before an assessment when possible. Late requests are considered but implementation for an imminent assessment is not guaranteed. Adjustments do not waive essential learning outcomes.

title: Counselling appointments
text: Students may book up to six confidential counselling sessions per semester through the wellbeing portal. Routine appointment requests normally receive an offer within five working days. Confidentiality has exceptions where disclosure is required to address immediate serious danger or another applicable obligation. The routine booking service is not an emergency response service; immediate danger should be directed to local emergency services.

title: Campus emergency reporting
text: For an immediate threat on campus, contact local emergency services and campus emergency security using verified official contact information. State your location, the nature of the incident, and whether anyone is injured. Move to safety if possible and follow responders' instructions. This fictional corpus deliberately supplies no operational telephone number and cannot determine the real services for a user's location.

title: Student club events
text: A recognized club must submit an event request at least ten working days before the event. Events with more than 100 attendees or external speakers require a risk review and at least fifteen working days' notice. Approval is required before advertising. The request must list an organizer, venue, expected attendance, accessibility arrangements, and budget.

title: Room booking for clubs
text: Recognized student clubs may request teaching rooms outside scheduled classes for up to three hours per booking. Requests should be submitted five working days in advance and require a named organizer. Teaching and accessibility arrangements take priority. A room reservation alone is not event approval; the student club event policy also applies.

title: Internship credit
text: An internship may earn three academic credits if approved by the program coordinator before work begins. It must include at least 120 supervised hours, a supervisor evaluation, and a reflective report. Paid and unpaid placements are eligible. Retroactive approval is not routine. Internship credit does not itself satisfy any immigration or professional licensing requirement.

title: Career advising cancellations
text: Students book career advising appointments through the careers portal. Cancel at least twelve hours in advance when possible. After two unexplained missed appointments in one semester, online booking is paused until the student contacts the careers office. The pause affects career advising bookings only, not course enrollment. Employers cannot access private advising notes without consent.

title: Laboratory safety induction
text: Students must complete a laboratory-specific safety induction before working in a laboratory. Access is limited to approved hours and trained users. Closed shoes and the protective equipment specified for the activity are required. Food and drink are prohibited. Report incidents and near misses immediately to the supervisor. Completion of a general online course alone does not grant unsupervised access.

title: Research participant data
text: Research involving human participants requires ethics approval before recruitment or data collection. Collect only data needed for the approved purpose and store identifying data separately with restricted access. Consent materials must explain withdrawal limits and retention. The default retention is five years after project closure unless the approved protocol or law requires otherwise. Removing names alone does not guarantee anonymity.

title: Campus shuttle
text: The fictional campus shuttle operates on teaching weekdays from 07:30 to 20:30, departing the central stop every 30 minutes. Service is suspended on public holidays unless a special notice is published. Boarding requires a valid campus ID. Wheelchair-accessible travel may be booked through transport with one working day's notice. This is a sample timetable, not a real transport service.

title: Meal plan changes
text: Students may change a semester meal plan once during the first ten teaching days. Changes take effect on the next working day after approval, and the price difference is charged or credited proportionally. Unused meal entries expire at semester end and are not transferable. Dietary accessibility requests are handled separately and may be raised throughout the semester.

title: Formal student complaints
text: Students may submit a formal service complaint within 30 calendar days of the event or discovery. The ombuds office acknowledges receipt within three working days and aims to provide an outcome within twenty working days. Complex cases may take longer with written updates. Retaliation for a good-faith complaint is prohibited. Grade appeals and emergency reports follow their own procedures.
